terms.gloss: the basics, the ABC, first principles
terms.comment: Properly the letters of the alphabet, then the first lessons of any art; the very basics are prīma elementa (Hor. S. 1.1.26; Quint. 1.2.26).

terms.gloss: basic, first, elementary (of lessons, rules, needs)
terms.comment: Latin says “first” where English says “basic”. Basic needs are the things ad vīctum necessāria (cf. Cic. Fam. 14.20; see necessary).
Augustan and later (Lewis & Short), most often of a soldier’s first service.

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.23: fundāmentum autem est jūstitiae fidēs
terms.comment: What everything else rests on, as a house on its foundations.

phrases.latin: ut puerīs ōlim dant crustula blandī doctōrēs, elementa velint ut discere prīma
phrases.english: as coaxing teachers sometimes give children biscuits, to make them willing to learn their ABC

phrases.latin: fundāmentum autem est jūstitiae fidēs, id est dictōrum conventōrumque cōnstantia et vēritās
phrases.english: the foundation of justice is good faith: standing by what has been said and agreed, and telling the truth

sources: Lewis & Short: elementum · Lewis & Short: primus · Lewis & Short: rudimentum · Lewis & Short: fundamentum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 28, 182, 185.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-horatius, loci-tacitus, loci-cicero-philosophica), checked against the editions named there.
